terms.definition: The minimum energy needed to remove an electron from the surface of a metal.
terms.examiner: Symbol φ on the data booklet; hf = φ + E_k(max).

terms.definition: The minimum frequency of light that will release electrons from the metal surface.
terms.examiner: f₀ = φ/h. Below it, no electrons are emitted however intense the light.

terms.definition: The minimum potential difference needed to stop the most energetic photoelectrons.
A packet (quantum) of electromagnetic energy, E = hf.
terms.examiner: One photon is absorbed by one electron: that is why intensity changes the number of electrons, not their maximum energy.

terms.definition: The energy gained by an electron accelerated through a potential difference of one volt: 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ J.
terms.examiner: Convert eV to J before using E = hf.
